nodes.description: Biallelic germline DIS3L2 variants (nonsense, frameshift, missense, and an exon 9 deletion generated by LINE-1 non-allelic homologous recombination) remove the 3'-5' exoribonuclease activity of DIS3L2. Unlike DIS3 and DIS3L1, DIS3L2 lacks the PIN domain and has a different intracellular localization.

The 7SL RNA of the signal recognition particle is a DIS3L2 substrate. In DIS3L2-deficient cells, persistently uridylated aberrant 7SL disturbs ER-targeted mRNA translation, ER calcium leaks, calcium signaling response genes are induced, and embryonic stem cell differentiation is perturbed. How this contributes to the patient phenotype is not known.

evidence.reference_title: Perlman syndrome: report, prenatal findings and review.

nodes.description: DIS3L2 degrades 3'-oligouridylated RNAs after uridylation by terminal uridylyl transferases. Its substrates include LIN28-directed uridylated pre-let-7 and a broad set of aberrantly processed, highly structured noncoding RNAs (7SL, RMRP, rRNA, snRNA, tRNA, Y RNAs). Loss of DIS3L2 stabilizes these substrates. Mature let-7 levels are not changed by DIS3L2 loss, so the disease mechanism is not thought to run through let-7 depletion.
